newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up after failure to break resistance.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up after failure to break resistance.

text.p: Brent crude futures prices in Asia were higher in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday in a modest rebound to the overnight failure to break support on the front-month contract.
March Brent, trading on SIMEX, last traded at $22.20 per barrel, up 15 cents from London's settlement but hardly changed from midday levels.
Brokers said they were finding some bids after the contract tested long-term front-month support at $22.00 overnight.
The level was December's low and at the time, represented a three-month low.
However, despite the modest support, brokers said the market remained fixed in a downtrend and they expected another test of $22.00 soon.
NYMEX March crude on ACCESS was last traded at $23.98 per barrel, up four cents from New York, and in the middle of the overnight trading range of $23.63 to $24.26.
February heating oil extended overnight gains after forecasts of below normal temperatures, but had not traded in Asia time since early morning.
February was last traded at 67.40 cents per gallon, up 0.11 from New York. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3081)
